name: doodad-flag-bits
description: Fix Doodads on Load: flag bits above 4 (0x08 to 0xff, inside and outside the playable area): the editor's save keeps bits 0 to 3 only (0x1e to 0x0e, 0x80 to 0x02); Studio's fixed-on-load save does the same

steps.eval: const s = await w3.services.get('w3.terrain'); for (let i = 0; i < 60 && !s.placedObjects()?.doodads?.length; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)); window.__driveEd.pushEdit({ undo() {}, redo() {}, terrain: false, objects: false });

name: doodad-scale-one-axis-zero
description: Fix Doodads on Load: a scale with one or two axes at 0. Destructables (LTbr, LTcr) get one random scale for all axes only when x is 0 (x nonzero: clamped x for all); doodads (LOch) a random value for each zero axis. The random picks differ by design (ignored in the compare: scales of destructables with x 0, zero axes of LOch); every other scale matches. Studio's picks are checked in its eval: each destructable with x 0 has one scale on all axes within its type's range (DestructableSkin.txt: LTbr 1.1 to 1.5, LTcr 0.8 to 1.2), each zero axis of LOch a value within 0.8 to 1.2 (DoodadSkins.txt); the World Editor's picks aren't checked

steps.eval: const s = await w3.services.get('w3.terrain'); for (let i = 0; i < 60 && !s.placedObjects()?.doodads?.length; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)); const d = s.placedObjects().doodads; const range = { LTbr: [1.1, 1.5], LTcr: [0.8, 1.2], LOch: [0.8, 1.2] }; const inRange = (id, v) => v >= range[id][0] - 1e-4 && v <= range[id][1] + 1e-4; const bad = []; for (const i of [0, 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15]) { const sc = d[i].scale; if (!(sc[0] === sc[1] && sc[1] === sc[2] && inRange(d[i].id, sc[0]))) bad.push(`${i} ${d[i].id} ${sc}`); } for (const [i, axes] of [[16, [0]], [17, [1]], [18, [2]], [19, [0, 1]], [20, [0]], [21, [1, 2]], [22, [1, 2]], [23, [0, 1]]]) { if (d[i].id !== 'LOch' || axes.some((a) => !inRange('LOch', d[i].scale[a]))) bad.push(`${i} ${d[i].id} ${d[i].scale}`); } if (d.length !== 24 || bad.length) throw new Error(`random scales outside their type's range (of ${d.length} doodads): ${bad.join('; ')}`); window.__driveEd.pushEdit({ undo() {}, redo() {}, terrain: false, objects: false });

name: doodad-scale-turned-range
description: a 0 scale of LTt0 (range 1 to 0.8, turned; destructable) with references in and out of the range. The random picks of the three x=0 cases differ by design (ignored in the compare); Studio's eval checks its picks: one scale on all axes within 0.8..1.0 (the World Editor's aren't checked); the others, 0.5 and 2 included, match

steps.eval: const s = await w3.services.get('w3.terrain'); for (let i = 0; i < 60 && !s.placedObjects()?.doodads?.length; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)); const d = s.placedObjects().doodads; const bad = [0, 1, 2].filter((i) => { const sc = d[i]?.scale ?? []; return !(sc[0] === sc[1] && sc[1] === sc[2] && sc[0] >= 0.8 - 1e-4 && sc[0] <= 1 + 1e-4); }); if (bad.length) throw new Error(`LTt0's random scales outside 0.8..1.0: ${bad.map((i) => `${i} ${d[i]?.scale}`).join('; ')}`); window.__driveEd.pushEdit({ undo() {}, redo() {}, terrain: false, objects: false });

name: units-on-ground
description: units on a slope, plateau, ramp, lake bed and in water (p8a: footmen, flyer, ship, barracks, start location): z of every unit as the editor saves it. The editor writes the newer format (subversion 11, itemTable and hero attributes), ignored here

steps.eval: const s = await w3.services.get('w3.terrain'); for (let i = 0; i < 60 && !s.placedObjects()?.units?.length; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)); if (!s.placedObjects()?.units?.length) throw new Error('the units never came'); window.__driveEd.pushEdit({ undo() {}, redo() {}, terrain: false, objects: false });
